text:
Maya: heads-up — customer acme-ops (support#4472) reports sudden p95/p99 regressions on /v1/generate. p95 ~220ms -> ~1.4s, p99 ~900ms -> ~3.2s over the last 18m. graphs show KV miss rate spikes aligned with the regression. anyone on call?
Alex: on it. any recent config/deploys to prefix normalization / cache eviction?
Maya: just rolled a small change to header-to-prefix canonicalization yesterday (olivia authored). not sure if related. noticed lots of unique cache keys in the metrics stream.
Olivia: that PR was limited to normalizing tenant headers -> prefix keys to reduce skew. it *should* reduce cardinality, not increase. putting up the diff now.
Samuel: can you paste a short example of keys that are thrashing? curious if session ids or sdk-generated uuids slipped into prefix.
Maya: logs show keys like: `tenant:acme-ops:route:v1:ctx:session=01f4b2-...` and `tenant:acme-ops:route:v1:ctx:session=01f4b3-...` — session id appears in prefix.
Olivia: oh — our normalization missed `ctx.session` in a nested header map for some SDKs. that would explode prefix cardinality.
Alex: that maps to warmup pressure: many new prefixes -> frequent KV misses -> heavy backend lookups -> latency spiral.
Samuel: repro steps I ran locally:
```
# hammer with varied session ids to mimic traffic
for i in {1..1000}; do
  curl -s -H "X-Session: session-$i" -H "X-Tenant: acme-ops" \
    -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
done
```
Observed backend qps spike, cache miss rate -> 98%, p95 ~1.2s.
Olivia: immediate mitigation options: 1) rollout hotfix to include `ctx.session` in normalization blacklist 2) increase prefix TTL so warmup cost spreads 3) enable soft-local eviction (prefer eviction without invalidation) 4) add short-term circuit-breaker for high-miss tenants.
Alex: for short-term customer impact, route acme-ops to a fallback path with a slightly higher throughput model (lower tail latency) until we patch. can we do that from routing layer?
Samuel: yes — policy can route by tenant; I'll create a canary route to model-x-small that has lower p99 in load tests.
Maya: infra-bot, can you show current prefix-cardinality and evictions for acme-ops?
infra-bot: prefix_cardinality_acme-ops: 182k (1h), avg_kv_miss_rate: 67%, evictions_last_30m: 42k, warmup_backoff: disabled
Olivia: 182k is huge — confirms session leakage.
Alex: action list: 
- Samuel: create route -> fallback model and enable for tenant (ETA 15m)
- Olivia: prepare normalization patch to blacklist nested session header and run fast canary (ETA 30m)
- Maya: notify support + customer and enable emergency throttle if needed (ETA 10m)
- Alex: add temporary TTL bump for prefix cache (increase from 60s -> 300s) to reduce churn (ETA 10m)
Samuel: applying route now. I'll keep an eye on p95/p99.
Olivia: starting a unit/e2e to reproduce normalization gap and will ship patch if green.
infra-bot: deploy triggered: route-update job #7823 -> canary on 2 nodes.
Maya: observing metrics — miss rate dropping to 34% after route change, p95 down to ~360ms. still above baseline but much better.
Alex: good. we should still push the normalization fix; routing is a bandaid. also consider adding a circuit-breaker that returns 429 when tenant miss rate > 80% for >2m.
Olivia: agreed. will include a test for nested hdrs and a follow-up to update docs for SDK header shapes.
Maya: I'll draft an incident note and tag postmortem if we confirm deploy regression.
Samuel: monitoring — will keep the route for 2h then reevaluate.
Maya: thanks all. I'll update support and close the customer loop once the normalization patch is live. :thumbsup:
Olivia: FYI — initial PR ready at https://git.redwood.ai/olivia/prefix-normalize-fix, running CI.
infra-bot: metric alert resolved for acme-ops (p95 < 500ms).
Maya: closing loop — customer notified, support ticket updated with mitigation steps and planned permanent fix. will keep postmortem on our radar.
Alex: leave a note to consider smarter key hashing for future: canonicalize tenant + route but hash session portion outside prefix if needed. avoids cardinality explosion.
Maya: noted. thanks everyone.
